Sorts the month ratings by average and returns the best player of a league, with an optional age filter.
`MONTH_RATINGS::find_best_player(league, age)`, used by the monthly award (`award_best_rated_player`). It sorts the table by average
(qsort `exe::crt_qsort` with 0x768200: those with fewer than 3 matches go to the end) and returns the first record of the
league (−1: any) with at least 3 matches (then 2, 1 and 0); with an age (not 0xff), those above it are only counted
and the youngest only qualifies after 3 have been counted; with a league, the current league of the person's club
(+0x39, +0x57) must also be the requested one. None: 0.

Daily fixture manager update: reserve fixtures, queued fixture news, removal of AI-only friendlies and cup round

thiscall, ret 4) and, on day 3, also for tomorrow;

asks for it and to the manager of the club in slot 1 if slot 0xf asks for it (`get_slot`: push k; mov ecx, news ->

3. days 5 and 6, if yesterday is in the same year: in yesterday's lists (the 3 slices, the key nations up to

Finds a new date for a fixture: within a window by fixture type, it tries weekdays in a fixed order and keeps the
first date with no (or tolerable) clash; otherwise 2 days later.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::find_new_fixture_date(fixture)`, used by calendar entry (`add_fixture`), by same-day clashes (`resolve_same_day_clash`)
and by rescheduling (`move_nearby_club_fixtures`); SEH frame only for the dates. Without a fixture: the box (as in the original). If
the units digit of the round (+0x30, `exe::comp_util_get_round_variant`: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl) is 3 or 4, the fixture's 15-byte record
goes into the leg check list [0xae2a48] (0x68d0d0). The window by type (+0x3a): 2, up to the date at +0x24/+0x26
(without it, the box and 2 weeks), starting 4 weeks later (if the end is more than 20 weeks away) or 3 days later; 4
and 6, from 3 days to 2 weeks; 5, from 0 to 1 week; 7, 8 and 10, from 3 days before to 1 week; the others, none. In
two passes (the second checking the two days before), through the weekdays in the order 2, 1, 5, 6, 0, 3, 4, every 4

+0x2a) and the time slot (+0x3f, `get_time_slice`); with no clash (`find_fixture_clashes`), or with severity 1 or below the type, it
stays. Not found: 2 days after the fixture's date (or after today, if it has already passed).

Adds a fixture to the calendar: fixes the stage, reschedules late fixtures, moves weekend league fixtures to the
home club's preferred day, resolves clashes, handles national team fixtures and neighbours, and puts the fixture in
the day list or in the other year's block.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::add_fixture(fixture, reset)`, used by the cups, leagues, friendlies and rescheduling (20 callers);
SEH frame for the dates and the new manager. `reset` zeroes the count of chained reschedulings (word [0xae2a40]). It
fixes the stage (`mark_calendar_year`: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl), +0x2e = −1; a fixture whose date has already passed and is
not played: new date (`find_new_fixture_date`). A league fixture of the home club's league (+0x57 or +0x60) with no round (+0x30,
+0x32) and no stage (+0x3b), once (bit 0x800 of +0x4d): on Saturday or Sunday, it moves to the home club's preferred
day (+0x72: 4, 5 or 6) if there is no clash there. With fewer than 10 chained reschedulings, the clashes (`find_fixture_clashes`):
severity 0x14, the same-day clash (`resolve_same_day_clash`) and 1; a cup or type 9 refused by the competition (+0x64): 0; severity
at least the type: 0 if the fixture's national team has a call-up ([0xb74434], 0x7e6f20), otherwise a new date and
it goes in again; otherwise it goes in (`insert_fixture`) and the clashing fixtures leave: the friendlies (`exe::friendly_is_friendly_competition`/`on_friendly_fixture_cancelled`
on [0xae2c74]), type 9 (`remove_fixture`), the others rescheduled (`remove_fixture`, `find_new_fixture_date`, `add_fixture`) with the news (`queue_fixture_moved_news` on
[0xae2a58]). In the block's year (+0x1130): the key nation (`comp_active_key_nation_of_fixture`), the order (`add_away_trip_illness_risk`), the national team
fixtures (`exe::reservecomp_add_b_or_under21_fixture` on [0xb74434], `select_squads_for_fixture` on [0xb74318]), the neighbours (`move_nearby_club_fixtures`, key 3 or 5); if it did not go
in, into the list of the day, slice and key (0x68d0d0). Outside the year, into the other year's block (+0x112c:
`set_year` for the year, or a new one of 0x1184 bytes, `exe::new_fixture_manager`; out of memory, the box and 0).

Switches a fixture block to another year: saves the year's fixtures, moves the other block to the neighbouring year
if needed, destroys the 366 days' lists, switches the year and leap flag, creates new lists and loads the new year's
fixtures.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::set_year(year)`, used by calendar entry (`add_fixture`, the other year's block), by saving and removing
fixtures and by the friendlies; SEH frame for the new blocks. If the same year (word, +0x1130): returns 1.
Otherwise: it writes the year's fixtures (`exe::fixture_manager_save_fixtures`: ecx = block; push 0 -> thiscall; on failure, the box and 0); if
the other block (+0x112c) is in the requested year, it moves to the year neighbouring this one's (`set_year` on it);
it destroys and frees the lists of the 366 days × 3 slices × key nations ([0xb64738], signed byte; `exe::drop_llist`,
`exe::crt_operator_delete`); the other block in the requested year, if this is the main one (+0x1183), is destroyed and freed
(`exe::drop_fixture_manager`: ecx = block -> thiscall; `exe::crt_operator_delete`); the new year, leap flag at +0x1132 (`exe::date_is_leap_year`: push year; add esp, 4
-> cdecl), the new lists (new 0xe: `exe::crt_operator_new`, push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; `exe::new_llist`: ecx = block -> thiscall; out of
memory, the box and 0) and the loading of the year's fixtures (`load_fixtures`: ecx = block -> thiscall). Returns 1.

`fix_man_load_club_dates()` (cdecl), from the calendar constructor (`exe::new_fixture_manager`, 0x5a9e38: on a new career and on
loading the save). With the table already allocated ([0xae2a5c]), the "Error" box for line 0xfe4. It allocates one
word per club (malloc `exe::crt_malloc` of 2 × [0xae235c]; out of memory, the box for line 0xfec); reads from
CM3_TEMP\club_dates.tmp ("rb", fread `exe::crt_fread`; a short read: the box for line 0xff6) and closes it; without the file
(a new career), it zeroes the table.

Writes the leg check list [0xae2a48] into CM3_TEMP\check_fixture_legs.tmp: the count (2 bytes) and the 15-byte
items.
`fix_man_save_fixture_leg_checks()` (cdecl), from the calendar save (0x5ac399): with the leg check list ([0xae2a48],
LLIST) empty (the count word zero), nothing. It writes into CM3_TEMP\check_fixture_legs.tmp ("wb") the count (2
bytes) and, from the start of the list (cursor +0xa ← head +2), each 15-byte item (`next_list_item`; a short write: the
"Error" box for line 0x10e0, and it carries on); then it closes the file. If the file does not open: nothing.

Resolves a new fixture falling on the same day as another: the one with higher priority stays and the other is moved
to a new date, with the rescheduling news.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::resolve_same_day_clash(fixture, clashes)`; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path. The
new fixture `fixture` falls on the same day as another, the first of the `clashes` list (cursor +0xa goes back to
the start +2 and `next_list_item` reads it); without either of them, the box for line 0xde6 and it returns 1. It copies both
(0x4f bytes) and finds the target weekday from the date of the list's fixture (+0x2a, +0x28; 0x549ef0, `exe::date_operator_3d`,
`exe::date_get_weekday`): days 0 and 5 of `exe::date_get_weekday` go to 6, 1 and 3 to 2, 2 to 1, 4 and 6 to 5 (`exe::date_get_nearest_weekday` gives the date). Each
one's priority is its competition's (+0x69 of +0x14), +0x15 (21) with a national team at home (+0x1c, `exe::database_is_national_team`); the
list's fixture leaves the day when the new one's priority is higher (or equal, with the new one's home club
reputation +0x80 higher) and it has not been played yet (+0x43 = 0xff): it is removed from the calendar (`remove_fixture`)
and the new one goes in (`add_fixture`); otherwise the new one leaves. The one that leaves gets the new date; with a
clash there (`find_fixture_clashes`, the list destroyed and freed: `exe::drop_llist`, `exe::crt_operator_delete`), a fixed fixture (+0x3a = 1) returns 0,
otherwise `find_new_fixture_date` finds another date; it goes into the calendar (`add_fixture`) with the rescheduling news (`queue_fixture_moved_news`,
caused by the other one). Returns 1.

Returns the club's first year with fixtures: 2001, or 2002 by bit 0 of its word in [0xae2a5c].
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::get_club_first_fixture_year(&id)`; this is not read. The first year with fixtures of club `[id]`:
2001, or 2002 with bit 0 of its word in [0xae2a5c]. Returns `ax` (the screen caller compares 16 bits).

Returns the club's last year with fixtures: its word in [0xae2a5c] without bit 0, or the current year.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::get_club_last_fixture_year(&id)`; this is not read. The club's last year with fixtures: its word
in [0xae2a5c] without bit 0 (halved); with no year, the current year [0xae2c92]. Returns `ax` (the screen caller
keeps 16 bits).

For a non-friendly fixture, moves the clubs' fixtures two days before one day earlier and those two days after one
day later, if the new date is free, with the news.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::move_nearby_club_fixtures(fixture)`, from adding the fixture (`add_fixture`); SEH for the local list
and the dates. A fixture of a friendly competition (+0x14, `exe::friendly_is_friendly_competition`): nothing. For both clubs (+0x1c, +0x20) of a
nation (+0x53) with the flag +0x11c: the club's first fixture two days before (`find_fixtures`, side 1), not a friendly and
with +0x43 = 0xff, moves to one day before it; the first fixture two days after, not a friendly, moves to one day
after it. Only if the new date has no other fixture (`find_fixture_clashes`): it removes (`remove_fixture`), adds (`add_fixture`, 0) and posts
the rescheduled fixture news (`queue_fixture_moved_news`, with the fixture as the cause).

Reschedules the club's fixtures from one day before to one day after a national team date: each removed fixture gets
a new date, is added back and posts the news with the old date.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::reschedule_club_fixtures_near_date(club, date)`, from the national team call-ups (0x777940: a club
with more than two players called up); SEH for the local list. The club's fixtures (the id in `*club`) from one day
before to one day after the date (`find_fixtures`, side 1); each one that leaves the calendar (`remove_fixture`) gets a new date
(`find_new_fixture_date`), goes back (`add_fixture`, 1) and posts the news with the old date (`queue_fixture_moved_news`, no cause).

Queues the "fixture moved" news: updates the new date of an existing news item for the same fixture, or queues news
1 with the fixture and the cause or the old date.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::queue_fixture_moved_news(fixture, cause, old date)`, from the reschedulings (`add_fixture`, `reschedule_club_fixtures_near_date`,
`resolve_same_day_clash`, `move_nearby_club_fixtures`); SEH for the local news. The queue at +0x1128 (created the first time: `exe::crt_operator_new` and `exe::new_llist`):
if there is already news for the same fixture, it only changes the new date (data 5 and 6); otherwise news 1: the
fixture (+0xc, +0x10, +0, +0x32, +0x30, the new date +0x2a/+0x28, +0x40, +0x41) and the cause (the same fields of it
in data 7 to 0xd) or, with no cause, −1 and the old date (data 0xc and 0xd); it goes into the queue (0x68d0d0,
0xdf).

to the start and walks). Null fixture or none equal: 0; out of memory for the year block: the box (line 0x7cf) and

Finds (or creates) the fixture's year block and appends a copy of the fixture to its day, slice and key-nation list.

day, slice and key nation in the year block (through the chain). Out of memory for the block: the box (line 0x3ff);
a failed copy: the box (line 0x3eb).

Removes the first item with the same bytes from the fixture's day, slice and key-nation list; returns 1 if removed.

year block, through the chain) the first item with the same bytes (`manager_manager_remove`). Returns 1 if removed, 0 if not; out of

Counts (and copies into the list, if given) the calendar fixtures between two dates in the key-nation lists of the
club or competition, with type, club side and competition filters.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::find_fixtures(day0, year0, day1, year1, club, list, comp, type, side)`: counts (and, with `list`,
copies into it) the calendar fixtures between (day0, year0) and (day1, year1) inclusive, day by day (366 per year),
in the three slices of each day and in the key-nation lists: the club's (index into [0xae23b4], 0x245 bytes; a
national team `exe::database_is_national_team`: nations 0 and 1; otherwise 2..7, the one from `comp_active_key_nation_of_club` and the partner `fix_man_get_partner_key_nation_index`, without
repeats) or only the competition's (`comp_active_key_nation_of_fixture`). Filters: type (0xfe any), club side (0xff any) and competition (−1
any). Returns the count (word); a failed copy shows the box (line 0x93b) and stops there. Hot (288 thousand calls up
to 2002-06-01): no counter.

Copies into the list the fixtures of one day and slice for the requested competition, round and type, and returns

postponement and from moving cup rounds to the fixed dates): copies into `list` the fixtures of the day and slice,
in the list of the competition's key nation (`comp_active_key_nation_of_fixture`; −1: nation 0), of the competition (+0; −1 any), of the round
(+0x34, word; −1 any) and of the type (+0x42; 0xfe any). Returns how many (word); a failed copy shows the box (line
0x634) and stops there.

Tells whether the competition has a fixture on the date in any of the three calendar slices.

used), from the European Championship qualifiers (0x57fd60): 1 if the competition has a fixture (+0 = comp) on the
date in any of the three slices of the calendar [0xae2a58], in its key nation's list (`comp_active_key_nation_of_fixture`). Competition −1 or
below: 0; null date: the box (line 0xe89) and 0.

Finds the next (or previous) fixture from a year/day/slice cursor, inclusive, matching the competition, stage and
two club filters; writes the cursor back and returns the fixture, or 0.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::find_next_fixture(year*, day*, slice*, forward, comp, stage, club_a, club_b, ...)`: the fixture
after (or before, `forward` 0) the cursor (year, day, slice), the cursor itself included, that passes the filter
(fixture_matches_next_filter: competition +0, stage +0x34 and the two clubs +0xc/+0x10, each -1 = any). The group of
lists comes from `comp_active_key_nation_of_fixture` (the competition of table [0xae23d0] + 107 × comp, 0). Forward: slices up to 2, days up to
365 (0x16e exclusive), following years from day 0 (the slice only goes back to 0 when the day turns); backward:
slices down to 0, then 2, days down to 0, previous years from day 0x16d. Five years from the cursor's year (forward:
signed less than unsigned; backward: signed), 0. Found: it writes the cursor (day, year and the slice as a byte) and
returns the fixture. The last 3 arguments are not read. The original passes `get_fixture_list` the year, day and slice with
the high half of locals that were never written (garbage), but it and what it calls (`set_year`, `exe::new_fixture_manager`, `exe::date_is_leap_year`)
only use the word/byte: the port passes zero. Used in the cup draws (Cup.cpp 0x519d90, `exe::cup_process_fixture`, `exe::cup_label_round_extra_fixtures`). No SEH,
no box (`get_fixture_list`'s only when out of memory).

Returns 1 when a fixture in the day lists uses the stadium, in the given slice or in slices 0 to 2 (slice -1).
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::is_stadium_in_use(stadium, day, year, slice)`: 1 if any fixture (+0x18 = the stadium, not null) in
the day's lists uses the stadium. The groups: 0 to 7 and the stadium's (`comp_active_key_nation_of_stadium`, byte), the latter skipped if it
repeats one of the eight. Slice -1 (byte): slices 0 to 2, otherwise only that one. The slice goes to `get_fixture_list` in the
low byte of the year argument (the original keeps the loop there: the 3 high bytes are the year's). Null stadium: 0.
Used when scheduling friendlies (friendly.cpp `add_friendly_match`, 0x5c75a0) and in `exe::reservecomp_schedule_reserve_fixtures`, `exe::reservecomp_add_b_or_under21_fixture`. No SEH, no locals
without a value.

Returns the fixture's time slice (1 weekend, 2 otherwise) by the competition's nation and the weekday.
`this` is not read. The time slice of a fixture of competition `comp` on day `day` (word): the Netherlands, Ireland,
Belgium and France (nation id +0x5d in [0x9cf338], [0x9cf2dc], [0x9cf244], [0x9cf300]) only have 1 on day 6; the
others, 1 on days 5 and 6; otherwise 2. Returns only `al`.

With the stadium in a third-world country, gives the visiting clubs the illness risk on the day before the fixture.
`FIXTURE_MANAGER::add_away_trip_illness_risk(fixture)`; `this` is not used. With the fixture's stadium (+0x18), its
city (+0x38) and the city's nation (+0x1f) in a third-world country (+0x7e = 3), each visiting club from another
nation (+0x53) — the home club (+0x1c, id +0xc) and the away club (+0x20, id +0x10) — gets the illness risk on the
day before the fixture.

a club from England ([0x9cf2e4]) or Wales ([0x9cf510]) (nation +0x53, id +0), the index of the other nation's active
key nation (the 35 records of 72 bytes at 0xb63d60: +0 the nation, active at +0x11c, +0x14 the index); otherwise

Returns the fixture list (`get_fixture_list` of the manager [0xae2a58]) for the year (+2) and day (+0) of the date, in the
given slice and group.
`get_fixture_list_for_date(date, slice, group)` (stdcall, ret 0xc): the fixture list from `get_fixture_list` of the manager
[0xae2a58] for the year (+2) and day (+0) of the date. The year argument carries in its high half that of the date
pointer (`mov ax, [eax+2]`), which is reproduced; the day argument carries the caller's ecx high half, which
`get_fixture_list` discards (`and 0xffff`): the port passes zero. Used on match days (set_up_the_day `set_up_the_day`, Rust, each list
of the day), in the friendlies (0x5cbf3e), in the human manager (0x5fe83a), in the media (0x7776a8) and in 0x7e6498,
0x7e6ac9.

Marks the fixture's year in both clubs' entries of the club dates table (year × 2 + bit, 2001 rule).
(cdecl) Marks the year (+0x28, word) of fixture `fixture` in the entries of the two clubs (+0xc and +0x10) of the
table [0xae2a5c] (words: year × 2 + bit 0). Empty entry: bit 0 is set, or the entry is zeroed in 2001, and the year
goes in; otherwise in 2001 bit 0 is cleared and the year goes up if larger. Null table: as in the original (error
box).

The end of the match day: frees the global list, the day's arrays and, for each match, the engine, the summary and

(`+0x5b`) and the object at `+0x5f` (`0x453bc0`); finally the match array.

Clears each of the day's matches' fields and picks the human's match (or the first marked one) for the screen.
Returns 1 if there was one of the human's.
With matches on the day (`+0x2b`), it clears the `0x40` bytes of each one (`+0xd`, `0x54` bytes, `+0x15` of them)

Starts the day's next match after the current one (`+0x2f`): skips the decided ones, those of a human club and those
already started; creates the engine and prepares it; in the 1st pass with none, moves to the 2nd. Returns 1 if it
started one.
Starts the next match of the day (`+0x19`, `0x69` bytes each, `+0x21` of them) after the current one (`+0x2f`; -2 =
finished). The current one still with an engine (`+0x57`): error `0x68d`. It skips those already decided (`+0x47`
-2), those with no match set in the 2nd pass (`+0x33` 1 and `+0x63.+0x10` zero), those of a human club (`0x600a50`
with `+0x44`/`+0x45`) and those already started (`+0x47` != -1, `+0x57`, `+0x53`).
On the chosen one: takes it off queue `[0xde2f70]` (`0x90d2f0` with -3), creates the engine (`0xf63b` bytes,
`0x6b7e50`; without it error `0x6b2` and it carries on) and prepares it (`0x6b7f20` with the fast mode from
`0x6b66a0`); `+0x2f` = it, returns 1. With none: in the 1st pass (`+0x33` 1) it moves to 2 and starts again from the
beginning; otherwise `+0x2f` = -2 and returns 0.

Moves the day's current match (`+0x2f`) forward: one engine step (1 in 3 or 6 calls, by the modes in `[0xae3138]`)
or to the end; when it finishes, creates the summary, records it, frees the engine and takes it off the queue.
Returns 1 if the match finished.
Without `ate_o_fim` (to the end), only 1 in every 3 (`0x40000` in `[0xae3138]+4`) or 6 (`0x80000`) calls, by counter
`[0xb67a54]` (0..100), and one engine step (`0x6b98c0` with 1); with `ate_o_fim`, steps (-1) to the end. The state
goes to `+0x67`; on finishing (2 or 8) it counts in `+0x25`, creates the summary (`+0x5f`, `0xd7a` bytes with 2
objects of `0x625` at `+0x11f`; without it error `0x713`), records it (`0x7293f0`), frees the engine and takes the
match off queue `[0xde2f70]` (`0x90d6b0`).

Closes one of the day's matches: copies the day's match into the fixture, records the result in the competition
(method 1, or the away-game path) and runs the post-match: players, events, contracts, suspensions, states, the
history and each side's club.
The closing of day match `p` (`0x69` bytes): copies the `0x4f` bytes from p+4 to the fixture (`+0`) and, with a
competition (`+0x14`), reads the round number of a human club (`[adadfc]` of the competition `+8`, `0x4a4850`,
`+0x2d` above 1; as in the original, it looks only at the away club `+0x20` on both passes) and records the result:
p+`0x47` = -3 (away game, `0x924050` with bits 12-13 of `+0x4d` and the copy with scores -1 in
`0x5ab510`/`0x5aa680`) or method 1 of the competition.
Then the post-match with the summary (p+`0x5f`): players (`0x6b6cc0`), events (`0x6b74a0`), contracts (`0x4ca6d0`),
suspensions (`0x55ca00`), `0x76b600` (except for -3), states (`0x62c080`) and, except for -3, the history
(`[0xb74434]` method 1, outside `[0x9cf684]`), `0x7c0d70`, `0x8c39f0`, `0x444930`, `0x868830`, `0x4134c0`,
`0x6951e0`, `0x59a5d0`, `0x7f8c00` and the club of each side (`0x6b79a0` with the round). Without `p`, error `0x73f`
and 0.

Plays the match day: on a network it ties the humans to their matches and plays them to the end; then plays each
match without an engine; finally closes each match, redoes the humans' stored tactics and frees the summaries.
Returns 1.
Convention: thiscall, `match_day.cpp`, ~3.3 KB. Plays day `dia` (`+0x19` matches of `0x69` bytes, `+0x21` of them,
`+0x25` finished, `+0x34` the human's). It starts the next one (`0x6b5a70`). On a network (`[0xa5a390]`): for each
pending match with a human (`+0x53`) it creates the humans' scoreboard (`+0x5b`, `0x11d` bytes), ties each human to
his side (`0x765480` `+0xe2`/`+0xe6`, `0x4542f0`, `0x727f00`), stores the highest level (`0x5fcff0`) and passes it
on (`0x5fd100`); then it notifies those not playing (`0x71b1b0`), releases the humans and plays their matches to the
end.
Then, each match still without an engine (`+0x47` -1): with a human on a network, it moves the current one to the
end (`0x6b5ce0`) and starts everything again; otherwise it creates the engine (`0x6b7e50`, `0x6b7f20`), plays to the
end (`0x6b98c0` -1, counting in `+0x25`), creates the summary (`0xd7a` bytes), records it (`0x7293f0`), frees the
engine and, if the engine was not in fast mode (`+0` of the engine zero), writes the score with the day's percentage
on the bar (`0x66f4e0`, `0x802f80`).
Finally it moves the current one (`0x6b5ce0` with 1), closes each match (`0x6b5f00`), redoes the humans' stored
tactics (`0x5fbe20`, `0x5fbd00`, `0x5b5960`) and frees the summaries; with a score written, the date on the bar
(`0x54ba20`).

Sets up the match day (date, mode 0..2): zeroes the arrays, gathers the pending matches of each list, records the
already decided ones, groups by list and by competition, points each match to its competition, creates the global
list and works out the day's interest. Returns the day.
Sets up day `dia` with the matches of date `data` in mode `modo` (0, 1 or 2; otherwise or with no date, error
`0x93`). Zeroes the day (`+0` mode; arrays `+1` groups of 24 bytes, `+0xd` competitions of `0x54`, `+0x19` matches
of `0x69`, each with capacity and count; `+0x2f` -1, `+0x33` 1).
For each of the `[0xb64738]` lists (`0x5ae6a0`): the pending matches (`+0x43` <= -1, except -2) go into the day
(copy of `0x4f` bytes; `+0x67` -1), those decided earlier (`0x923630` bit 0) are recorded and marked -2 (`0x923cc0`,
`0x5ab510`/`0x5aa680`), the others notified (`0x79c7b0`); the list's group (`0x48dcd0`) stores the range of its
matches, which is sorted (qsort with `0x6b6510`) and split by competition (`+4` of the copy), and each match points
to its own (`+0x63`).
Finally the global list `[0xb67dc8]` (`0x68d020`) and the day's interest (`0x6b5040`). The arrays grow 5 at a time
(`0x945667`; out of memory, errors `0xd6`, `0xf4`, `0x140`).

The current human leaves the match he was watching; with no other human watching, the match runs to the end, is
recorded and leaves the queue.
The current human (`[0xb77c7a]`) leaves the match he was watching (called only when a network player leaves,
`0x838c00`). His match (`[0xb74c26 + 0x300 × turn]`, `0x765480` → `+0xe2`): if another of the 16 humans (the last 16
records of `[0xae23bc]`, 110 bytes, `+0x5f` active) watches the same one and it is his turn (`0x7fffa0` on the
manager), it leaves silently; otherwise it removes the turn from the four arrays of the summary (`+0x5b`:
`+5`/`+0x45`/`+0x85`/`+0xc5`, the counters `+0x105..+0x108`).
Nobody else watching: it creates the engine (`+0x57`, `0xf63b` bytes, `0x6b7e50` + `0x6b7f20`; without it error
`0xa4b`), runs to the end (`0x6b98c0` with −1; state `+0x67`, 2 or 8 count in `[[0xb67a50]+0x25]`), except for 8
creates the summary (`+0x5f`, `0xd7a` bytes with 2 objects of `0x625` at `+0x11f`; without it error `0xa68`) and
records it (`0x7293f0`), frees the engine and takes the match off queue `[0xde2f70]` (`0x90d6b0`).

Finds in the fixture list the match of a statistics record (date, competition and club) and copies the fixture.
Returns 1 if found.
The fixture (`0x4f` bytes) of record `k` of the statistics index (`[this]`, 12 bytes: `+0` competition, `+4` one of
the clubs, `+8`/`+0xa` the date): it asks the schedule `[0xae2a58]` (`0x5acbe0`) for the matches of that date and
competition in a local list (`0x68d020`) and copies to `saida` the first one with club `+4` at home (`+0xc`) or away
(`+0x10`). Index outside 0..`[this+0x1c]` or null output: the original routine runs (error box, 0).

One step of the human's match on a network, by the clock and the humans' scoreboard (everyone sees each state;
sounds, events, engine step, end, half time, goals, minute); records it and picks the day's human match. Returns 1
if it changed.
One step of human match `p` on a network, by the clock (`0x90c510`) and the humans' scoreboard (`+0x5b`: `+0` state,
`+1` event, `+0x85` who has already seen it, `+0x105` humans, `+0x107` seen, `+0x108` pause, `+0x109` wait, `+0x10d`
time, `+0x111` may advance, `+0x115` highlight). Without `p`, it moves the current one (`0x6b5ce0`) and starts the
next (`0x6b5a70`).
It waits for everyone to see the state; then the sounds (`0x6d8c70`) and the time; it shows the next event
(`0x6d78b0`, highlight by table `0x6d5cd0`) or takes one engine step (`0x6b98c0` with 1) and sets the state: end
(2/8), half time (4), goals on each side (`+0xf5bd`/`+0xf5f3` against the summary), highlight, `+0x8eb2`, the minute
(`+0x8ed0` / 11) against the summary (wait `0x226` - 50 x `+0x51`); with a state, it records it (`0x729ff0`) and the
day's human match (`+0x34`) becomes the one with the highest competition (`0x6b6570`) or the furthest along.

Each human confirms the network match; with all of them confirmed, creates the engine and prepares it for watching,
or plays it to the end and records it.
The current human (`[0xb77c7a]`) confirms match `p` on a network (humans' scoreboard `+0x5b`: `+0x45` who confirmed,
`+0x105` humans, `+0x106` confirmed). With all: it creates the engine (`0x6b7e50`) and prepares it for watching
(`0x6b7f20` with the last argument 1). If it is not one to be watched (returns 0), it plays to the end (counting in
`[0xb67a50]+0x25`), creates the summary, records it (`0x7293f0`), frees the engine, takes it off the queue and sets
`+0x119`; if it is, it notifies the commentator (`+0x8f7a` = 3), creates the summary, records it for watching
(`0x729ff0`) and returns 1. Errors `0x4b8` (no match), `0x4d0`, `0x4ea`, `0x511` (out of memory).

the number by code (0: 5/4, 1: 11/10, 0x1ef: 1/0, 0x3de: 3/2, 0x483: 7/6, 0x528: 9/8; the first with the second

`Media::process_transfer_interest()` (SEH frame without a destructor on the normal path), called by the daily
routine (0x5cdd8f): drops transfer interest older than 31 days and, by chance, publishes the rumour linking the
player to the interested clubs, with the transfer request, the AI manager response, the squad reaction and the rival
warning; the AI owner may say he will not sell.
For each interest record (25-byte vector at [this+0xc], count [this+0x14]: +0 player, +4 club, +8 date, +0x10 state,
+0x11, +0x15): expired (more than 31 days, `exe::date_add_days`), no manager at the owning club (the +0xcf of the club of the
player's contract, kept from the previous iteration when he has no contract) or no player sheet: it leaves (the last
one takes its place). Otherwise, if the club can reach the player (`can_club_bid_for_player`): state 0 and draw(25) zero give the
rumour: the up to 5 clubs interested in him (records of the same player still at 0, marked 1; one already marked
cancels), news item 0xfbc (`construct_news_item`) with the player, the owner, the transfer request (below 15 in +0x5b and +0x59,
reputation above draw(12500) and +0x15 above 12.5 × +0x59 + 500: 0x24, otherwise draw(3)), +0x11, the AI manager's
response (`pick_ai_manager_response`), the strengths (`staff_get_player_strength_flags`), the exe::formation_get_position_mask(`position_mask`), the owner's manager, the transfer list
(`staff_is_transfer_listed_or_requested`) and the interested clubs by reputation; to the humans (`exe::transfer_manager_collect_player_news_recipients`: the interested ones and the humans of
the same division, or of the same nation and up to 3000 below) (`send_to_club_manager`); with the request, the squad reaction
(`apply_squad_reaction_to_player_story`); with the response, the rival warning (`warn_squad_of_position_rival`) and the reply to the story (`exe::media_apply_player_story_response`).
In state 1, an AI owner, the record date after the player's +0x3e, the contract without +0x49 and off the list,
happiness above draw(50) + 40 and draw(30) zero: the news that he will not sell (`news_create_not_for_sale_story`) and his records go to 2.
At the end, the vector is sorted (`exe::crt_qsort` with `compare_id_pair_keys`).

`news_create_not_for_sale_story(player, club, chairman, other)` (cdecl; media.cpp in the flow, european_cup.cpp in
the map, with no other caller; SEH frame without a destructor on the normal path): news item 0xfbe that the club
will not sell the player.
With a player sheet and a club, news item 0xfbe (`construct_news_item`) with the player, the other club (or −1), the club and a
draw(3); the chairman, if he likes the player (`exe::staff_is_favoured_by`) or with draw(+0x16 of his sheet) above draw(20), otherwise
−1 in slot 7; reputation (+0xd of the sheet) above 8000: to all managers (`send_to_all_managers`), otherwise to the interested
human managers (`exe::transfer_manager_collect_player_news_recipients` with 0xd8, up to 30, `send_to_club_manager`).

`Media::queue_trophy_praise_story(club, competition, flag)` (SEH frame without a destructor on the normal path),
called by the title records (0x8693e2, 0x86b000): news item 0x2e with the board and fans praising the manager for
the title.
A club with a manager, a competition and outside national sides: news item 0x2e (`construct_news_item`) with the manager, the
club, the competition, a draw(2), the outlet (`media_pick_outlet_type_for_club`), the pundit (`pick_random_pundit` with the nation or −1), the flag, the
board confidence (+6 of the row in [0xb67a44], or 5000), the club's league and the manager's days (`exe::date_days_since`); with
180 days or more, the club's reputation and the delivery to the manager (`send_to_club_manager`).

after a story about the player (the transfer rumour): the dislike chance from the interested clubs (Old Firm, league
fixture, rival, same division), the club rejecting him and, for each squad, staff and board member, a score from
squad status, ambition, loyalty and preferences; when drawn, the person comes to dislike the player and his contract
gets flag 1 or the 0x800 complaints

with a high-reputation player linked to the club and more than two squad players in his position: the unsettled
position rivals (by ambition and loyalty, by a draw) get contract flag 0x800, and the first one gives story 0x25

`media_format_response_option_label(type, option, out, size)` (stdcall, ret 0x10): writes the label of a media story
response option ("Deny rumour", "Defend Player", "No Comment"...) from the 22-case table by story kind into the
output (0x66f4e0), for the stories screen (0x742b3b, with 0xde1f64 and 0x7d0). A null output or a size below 15:
nothing.

`Media::process_transfer_squad_reactions(player, new, old, flag)`, at the end of each transfer
(TRANSFER_MANAGER::move_player_to_club, 0x8ca879): the squad reactions to the transfer. Only for a player (sheet
+0x61) aged 19 or more with reputation 4250.
(A) The media story at the front of the queue (0xbd0, +0x11 = 0x25, new club with id 0x25; never in practice):
grievances in its person's contract. (B) In the new club's squad (50 slots +0xd7), those who have been there more
than +0x5a + 15 days (`exe::date_days_since` of +0x3e) and have a contract: flag 0x800 with the same position turns into a
grievance (`exe::staff_contract_apply_event_flags` 0x80000000) and draws; 0x400 is cleared with a strong squad (`database_count_club_squad` up to the limit by
reputation); with more than 2 in the position, the strong player may become a grievance or flag 0x200; grievance
0x20000000 is cleared (`exe::staff_contract_clear_grievances`) when someone bigger arrives. A star signing (player's +0xd above 6250): the
supporters (+8 of the club's row in [[0xb67a44]], +500 up to 10000) and the celebration (`queue_signing_celebration_story`); if something
changed, draw(3) and the spokesman celebrate.
(C) In the old club's squad (with a league), with the club's strength and reputation (or the nation among the seven
at 0x9cf31c..): grievances 0x40000000 / 0x20000000 at the team mate leaving, morale −25, flag 0x400, flags
0x200/0x800 and grievance 0x80000000 cleared; if something changed and the player was a star, the unsettled team
mate (`queue_sale_unrest_story`).

`Media::queue_signing_celebration_story(player, club, type, a, spokesman)` (SEH frame for the local news item),
called by the transfer reactions (`process_transfer_squad_reactions`): news item 0xbe5 of the fans or a squad spokesman celebrating the
signing, to the club manager.
A player with +0x1a, a current club (+0x39) with a manager (+0xcf) and +0x69, a player sheet (+0x61); type 2 without
a spokesman: nothing. The news item 0xbe5: the player (id and the three keys), his club's id, draw(2), the outlet
(`media_pick_outlet_type_for_person`), the pundit (`pick_random_pundit` with the club, the outlet and the nation +0x53 or −1), the exe::formation_get_position_mask(`position_mask`),
the type, the computer manager's response (`pick_ai_manager_response` with 0x82; 0 with a human manager), for type 2 the spokesman (id
and keys), the club's reputation above 7250, the manager (id and keys) and `a`; it goes to the manager of the
player's club (`send_to_club_manager`).

`Media::queue_sale_unrest_story(old, new, player, team_mate)` (SEH frame for the local news item), called by the
transfer reactions (`process_transfer_squad_reactions`): news item 0xbe4 of the team mate unhappy at the sale, to the old club's manager.
An old club with a manager (+0xcf), not a national side (`exe::database_is_national_team`), a team mate and a player with a player sheet
(+0x61). The news item 0xbe4: the manager, the team mate and the player (id and the three keys of each), the ids of
the two clubs, draw(2) (+2 if the team mate's +0x5b is not above draw(5) + 10), the outlet (`media_pick_outlet_type_for_club`), the pundit
(`pick_random_pundit` with the nation +0x53 or −1) and 2; it goes to the old club's manager (`send_to_club_manager`).

`media_pick_outlet_type_for_person(person)` (cdecl): picks the media outlet type like the club version does, but
from the player's reputation (+0xb of the player sheet +0x61).
Used by the player's stories (`exe::media_create_player_media_story`): the outburst, the praise, wanting to play, and the signing celebration
(`queue_signing_celebration_story`, in transfers).

`Media::adjust_supporter_confidence(club, subject, topic, target, variant)` (SEH frame without a destructor): adds
the change to the supporters' confidence (+8 of the club's row in [[0xb67a44]], kept between 1 and 10000): the
target minus the current confidence, × 0.75, damped by a favoured or rejected manager and beyond ±1000 (see
`fan_confidence_change`).
Beyond ±500, news item 0xbe0 (local) to the club's manager (`send_to_club_manager`): 0 = 0, 1 = topic, 2 = variant, 3 = draw(4), 4
= club id, 5 = the degree (5 below −750, 4 negative, 3 up to 750, 2 above), 6..9 the manager; with a subject, 10..13
the subject and 14 = 6 favoured, 7 rejected, 8 neither; then −1, the new confidence and 0.

`Media::adjust_board_confidence(club, subject, topic, target, variant, sixth)` (SEH frame without a destructor):
adds the change to the board's confidence (+6 of the club's row, kept between 1 and 10000): (confidence − 6000)/20 +
target, × 0.75, damped by a chairman who likes or dislikes the manager and beyond ±1000 (see
`board_confidence_change`).
Beyond ±500, news item 0xbe0 (local) to the club's manager (`send_to_club_manager`): 0 = 1, 1 = topic, 2 = variant, 3 = draw(4), 4
= club id, 5 = the degree (5 below −750 with confidence below 4500; 9 when negative with confidence above 6250,
otherwise 4; 2 above 750 with confidence above 6250, otherwise 3), 6..9 the manager; with a subject 10..13 and 14 =
6/7/8 (the chairman likes, dislikes, neither); then the chairman (or −1), the new confidence, the sixth (with it 1
and the word +0xe), and the subject's flags: contract 0x10/0x20 above 25 years old, average rating above the league
average × 5, +0x59 and +0x5b above 14, more than 1500 days at the club, value (`calc_player_value`) above 4,500,000 and
reputation (+5 of the sheet) above 140.

`Media::queue_player_gratitude_news(player, club, type, variant)` (SEH frame without a destructor): posts news item
0xbda of the player's gratitude to the manager.
With a player with a sheet (+0x61), a club with a manager (+0xcf) and his contract with the club (`exe::contract_manager_get_contract_for_club`), news
item 0xbda (local) to the manager (`send_to_club_manager`): 0..3 the player (3 = −1 without +0xc), 4 = club id, 5 = the type, 6 =
the variant, 7 = the type's draw, 8..0xb the manager, 0xc = 0x420e9, 0xd..0x10 the assistant (+0xd3) or −1. The
type: if the player is on the media list (this +0/+8, 0x17 bytes, id at +8 and flag 2 at +0x10) or the contract has
0x2000 or 8 in +0x45, types 0, 2, 4, 7, 9, 0xe and 0x23 become 0x12 (+0x5d ≥ draw(10)) or 0x21; injured (`exe::injury_get_player_injury`):
0xc. For types 0, 6, 14 and 17: with the sheet's +0x44 below 10, draw(3) + 2; otherwise draw(5), and 0 or 1 raises
the sheet's +0x44 (up to 20).

`Media::post_player_backing_request_news(player, club, type, fourth)` (SEH frame without a destructor): for a human
club, posts news item 0xbcf of the player asking for backing to the manager.
With a player with a sheet (+0x61) and a human club (`exe::human_manager_is_human_club`), news item 0xbcf (local) to the club's manager
(`send_to_club_manager`): 0..3 the player (3 = −1 without +0xc), 4 = club id, 5/6 = (1, ·) with reputation (+0xb of the sheet)
above 4250, otherwise (2, ·): the second is 1 if (+0x57 > 15 and +0x5d < 6, or +0x5b < 10 and +0x59 < 6 in the lower
band), 3 if the type is 0x20, 1 or 0x1e with +0x59 > 15, +0x5b > 10 and more than 210 days at the club, otherwise 2;
7 = type, 8 = fourth, 9 = transfer listed (`staff_is_transfer_listed_or_requested`).

`Media::post_player_criticism_reaction_news(player, club, topic, response)` (SEH frame without a destructor): posts
news item 0xbdc of the player's reaction to criticism, delivered to the managers of the interested clubs.
With a player with a sheet, a club with a manager and the contract (`exe::contract_manager_get_contract_for_club`), news item 0xbdc (local): 0..3 the
player, 4 = club id, 5 = the reaction (with reputation above 4250 and above the club's, category `contract_category` 1 or 2 and
more than 22 years old: 1 or 3 if +0x59 < 10, +0x57 > 15 and +0x5d < 6; 2 or 4 with more than 1000 days, +0x59 > 15
and without 0x181 in the contract's +0x45; the higher one when the contract has 0x2000 or 8, +0x5b < 10, +0x5d > 10,
+0x59 < 15, more than 23 years old and the response is 2; otherwise 0), 6 = response, 7 = board confidence below
4000, 8 = topic, 9..0xc the manager. It goes to the managers of the clubs that `exe::transfer_manager_collect_player_news_recipients` ([0xde1f54], 0x21a, up to
30) returns.

`Media::rate_player_form_for_story(player, club, contract, type, mode, weight)`: the player's rating (x87, in st0)
for a media story kind.
Without a contract, the player's contract with the club (`exe::contract_manager_get_contract_for_club`); without any, 0. Base: the league's average
rating x ([0xb74350] +0x10 / +0x18, without games 6.8), the player's statistics (`get_stat`, category 6: s1 field 1,
s2 field 0x11, s3 field 2, default 6.5) and the average of the ratings (`ratings_average`) × 0.2: r = (s2 − x) + (average −
x) − weight/60; with s1 < 12, r × s1/12; when negative, × the ratio of the reputations. Then, by type (0..0x52),
additions from the contract type (+0x4f >> 4), the age, the days at the club (`exe::date_days_since`), attributes of the record
+0x61 and the weight; type 0x52 gives r × 0.75 + s3/max(s1, 1) − 0.4.

`Media::write_financial_trouble_news_text(news, body, out)`: writes the headline or body of the
club-in-financial-trouble story, by severity, with the club name linked.
It reads fields 0 (the club), 1 (the severity) and 2 of the news item (`get_slot`), builds the text in 0xde1f64
(0x66f4e0) by severity (> 0x1a5e, > 0xcb2 in the body; > 0x1a5e in the headline) with the club's name (+0x38) and
gender (+0x52), puts it into `out` (0x4ae660) and links the name to the club (0x4ae8a0, type 0x7d5).

`Media::log_story(a, b, type, subtype, response)`: appends a story to the story log and sorts it again.
Appends to the story log ([this], capacity +4, count +8; 23-byte records) today's date (+0, `exe::date_operator_3d` from
[0xae2c90]), the id of `a` (+8) and of `b` (+0xc) (−1 without them), the `type` (+0x13), the `subtype` (signed byte,
as a word at +0x11) and the `response` (+0x10); the count goes up and the log is re-sorted (qsort `exe::crt_qsort` with
`compare_story_log_records`). Without a log, it allocates 20 (`exe::crt_malloc`; without memory, box 0x6e11 and the end); when full, it grows by
20 (realloc `exe::crt_realloc`; box 0x6e1c).

`Media::expire_story_log()`: removes the stories older than the limit, moving the last one into the gap, then sorts
again.
Each story in the log older than the limit (today − 100 days; the team one, type 0xbdf, today − (40 + draw(40)), one
draw `exe::utils_random` per such story on each pass; dates from 0x54c8e0 over [0xae2c90]) is overwritten by the last one (23
bytes), the count goes down and the same place is looked at again. If any are left, it re-sorts (qsort with
`compare_story_log_records`). Without a log, nothing.

`Media::has_logged_story(a, b, type, subtype, since)`: tells whether a story is in the log.
The team story (type 0xbdf): a linear search for one of type 0xbdf with the id of `b` (+0xc) and the `subtype` (word
+0x11), without looking at `a` or the date: 1 if found. The others: a binary search (bsearch `exe::crt_bsearch` with `compare_story_log_records`)
by the key {id of `a` or −1, id of `b`, type, subtype} (the default date `exe::date_date_54a110` in the key, which the comparison
does not read); found and without `since`, 1; with `since`, 1 if the story is not older than it. Otherwise 0. `b`
cannot be null (the original reads it without checking).

`Media::add_transfer_interest(player, club, fee, valuation)`: if the {player, club} key is missing, appends the
interest and sorts again.
With the interest vector ([this+0xc], capacity +0x10, count +0x14; 25-byte records), it searches (bsearch `exe::crt_bsearch`
with `compare_id_pair_keys`) for the key {player id, club id or −1}: already there, nothing. Otherwise it appends: player id (+0),
club id (+4, read without checking), today's date (+8, `exe::date_operator_3d` from [0xae2c90]), 0 (+0x10, the rumour has not come
out yet), the `fee` up to 50,000,000 (+0x11) and the `valuation` × 100 truncated (+0x15, _ftol 0x945640); the count
goes up and it re-sorts (qsort with `compare_id_pair_keys`). Without a vector, it allocates 20 (`exe::crt_malloc`; without memory, box
0x665d and the end); when full, it grows by 20 (realloc `exe::crt_realloc`; box 0x6668). The key's default date (`exe::date_date_54a110`) is
on the stack, as in the original.

`compare_story_log_records(a, b)` (cdecl): the qsort and bsearch comparison of the story log.
Null first (`a` null −1, `b` null 1); by subject a (+8), subject b (+0xc) and type (+0x13), the difference of the
first one that differs; when equal, the difference of the subtypes (signed words +0x11).

`Media::remove_transfer_interest(person)`: removes the person's interests, moving the last one into the gap, then
sorts again.
In the interest vector ([this+0xc], [this+0x14] records of 25 bytes), each one of the person (+0 = id) is
overwritten by the last one (6 dwords and a byte), the count goes down and the same place is looked at again. If any
are left, it re-sorts (qsort `exe::crt_qsort` with `compare_id_pair_keys`).

`media_queue_player_apology_news(player, club, story)` (stdcall, ret 0xc; SEH frame without a destructor), called by
the story effects (0x736c00) and the reply to the player's story (`exe::media_apply_player_story_response`): builds news item 0xbdb and sends it to
the club's manager.
With the player, the sheet (+0x61) and the club, news item 0xbdb in a local (`construct_news_item` with 0) with the data 0 = id,
1 to 3 = the names (+0x33 of +4, +8 and +0xc; without the third, −1), 4 = club id, 5 = the story, 6 = 0 and 7 = the
variant: draw(4) for stories 0, 2 to 5, 13, 14, 17 and 35 (table 0x72bd2c), otherwise 0; it goes to the club's
manager (`send_to_club_manager`).

Draws a former international as the pundit for `club` (or to talk about `subject`), weighted by nation reputation
and caps (`this` is not read).
150 rounds; in each it draws people (`exe::utils_random` with [0xae2364], 110 bytes in [0xae23bc]) until it finds one aged
(+0x18) ≥ 37, with national team caps (+0x22) ≥ 50, a sheet (+0x69), no club (+0x39) if he has a contract (+0x61)
and who is not the club's manager (+0xcf); the 100th try ends the round. The weight is a draw of the nation's
reputation (+0x1a, word +0x8e) × caps, doubled if he is from the subject's nation (without a subject: he must be
from the club's nation, +0x53). From another nation: the reputation must beat 6500 + a draw of 100, the sheet's +0xc
≥ 6000 and the subject must not dislike him (`exe::staff_is_disliked_by`). The one with the highest weight is kept (the first accepted
always gets in). Without a club and without a subject: 0.

`Media::pick_ai_manager_response(manager, player, type)` (3.7 KB): the computer manager's response (1, 2 or 3) to a
story of the given type about the player.
Without a manager, without the manager sheet (+0x69), a player without a sheet (+0x61), the manager himself, without
a club (+0x39, otherwise the national side +0x24) or without the player's contract with it (`exe::contract_manager_get_contract_for_club`): 3. The rating
is trunc(5 × `rate_player_form_for_story`(player, club, contract, type, 3, 0)); without a player, the argument's word stays in its place
(the manager pointer, as in the original). Then, by type: 0x83 by the contract type and the knowledge (`exe::non_player_attribute_rating`);
0x82 by the manager's likes and dislikes (`exe::staff_is_disliked_by`/`exe::staff_is_favoured_by`) and draws; 0x1f by the transfer list (`staff_is_transfer_listed_or_requested`) and the
contract; the others, first, by the likes and dislikes with the rating, and then by families of types, each with its
own chain of draws (`exe::utils_random`); 8/0x25 and 3/4 can put the player on the manager's rejected list (`exe::staff_add_disliked_staff`).

`Media::post_financial_trouble_news(club)` (SEH frame without a destructor): posts news item 0x1790 of the club in
financial trouble to the managers of the nation, or to all for a big club.
With the club, the nation (+0x53), the sheet (+0x69, with +0x38) and the division (+0x57), it builds news item
0x1790 in a local (`construct_news_item` with 0) with the data 0 = club id, 1 = reputation (+0x80) and 2 = draw(2) (`exe::utils_random`); a
club with reputation 9000 or more in a division with +0x69 above 12: to all managers (`send_to_all_managers`); otherwise to those
of the nation (`send_to_nation_managers`). The local news item is 0xe0 bytes (the delivery copies only up to +0xde).

`Media::pick_rival_manager_id(club)`: returns the id of the manager of a rival of the same league and much bigger,
or of a drawn club in a league clash, who passes the draws; or −1.
With a manager (+0xcf) with a contract (+0x69) and a league (+0x57; without a league, only a national side,
`exe::database_is_national_team`): the first of the manager's rejected list (`staff_get_disliked_staff`) with a manager record and rating + 750 < rating
(never: the draw(3) there does not happen); then each rival (+0xb3, +0xb7, +0xbb) with a manager who passes the
draws, of the same league and with reputation (+0x80) above the club's + 750, with draw(3) ≠ 0; then up to 50 drawn
clubs (from [0xae235c] − 2 × [0xae2350]) that make a league clash (`comp_util_get_league_clash_type`, with the draw limit as 3rd argument, a
leftover on the original's stack) with a manager who passes the draws. Returns the manager's id, or −1.

`Media::queue_manager_fa_complaint_story(club, person, type, a, b, c)` (SEH for the local news item, no destructor),
called by discipline (0x55e300) and by MANAGER_MANAGER (`exe::manager_manager_handle_fa_request`, 0x6ab800): posts news item 0x178e of the manager's
complaint to the FA.
A club with a nation (+0x53) and a manager (+0xcf), and a person: news item 0x178e (the club; the manager, id and
keys, or −1; the type; the person, id and keys; a; b; the nation or −1; c) to the nation's managers (`send_to_nation_managers`) if
the reputation (+0x80) is above 4750, otherwise to the club (`send_to_club_manager`).

Picks a random pundit: type 1 on Sunday becomes 7; local types (2, 4): the club's pundits; the others: of the type
and nation (−1 any); up to 20, random(n) and the id, or −1.
Ret 0xc; 0x1094-byte frame through 0x945610: `PunditList::pick_random_pundit(club, type, nation)`, from the press
stories (`exe::media_create_player_media_story`, 0x733a60) and from the news texts. Type 1 on Sunday (0x54a3f0 = 6) becomes 7. Types 2 and 4
(local): those of list `[this+4]` whose +0xcb is the id of `[[club+0x69]+0x38]` (none: −1); the others: those of
list `[this]` of the type (+0xca) and the nation (+0xcf; −1 accepts any). Up to 20; none: −1; otherwise the id (word
+0, signed) of one of them by random(n).

Returns the name (+2) and flag (+0xd3) of the pundit with the id, or the default outlet type name and flag 0.
Ret 0x10: `PunditList::get_pundit_name(type, id, name, flag)`, from the news texts. Without `name`: flag 0. Id −1:
the type's default name and flag 0. Otherwise the pundit with the id (word +0) in list `[this+4]` (types 2 and 4) or
`[this]`: the name (+2, sprintf "%s" 0x944c9f) and the flag (+0xd3); without him, the default name and flag 0.

Fills the match record as seen by the club: date, fixture id, competition, venue, club, opponent and goals for and
against (the extra-time score, if any).
`fill_match_record_from_fixture(match, club, out)`, from the tactic statistics (`record_tactic_result`, at the end of each match
without a human) and from the records. Null match, club or output: the box (lines 0x29, 0x31, 0x39) and 0. Otherwise
the date (+0, `exe::date_operator_3d` of the Date(day +0x2a, year +0x28) from 0x549ef0), +8 the match id (+0), +0xc word +0x32,
+0xe word +0x30, +0x10 the side (`comp_util_get_fixture_venue_side`, cdecl(club, match)), +0x11 the club id, +0x1b dword +8 of the match; home
side (+0x1c): +0x15 the match's +0x10 and the score (+0x19 for, +0x1a against) from the extra-time one (+0x47/+0x48)
if it is not negative, otherwise the normal one (+0x43/+0x44); away side: +0x15 the +0xc and the score reversed.
Returns 1.

Stores the three name ids (−1 when missing), the person's id and birth date in a compact reference.
`fill_staff_name_ref(person, out)`, from the club and competition records, the suspension news, the award and the
player search. Null person or output: the box (lines 0x80, 0x88) and 0. Otherwise +0, +4, +8 the name ids (+4, +8,
+0xc of the person; −1 with no name), +0xc the person's id and +0x10 the birth date (+0x10, `exe::date_operator_3d`); returns 1.

Returns the result code of the record: 3 win, 2 score draw, 1 goalless draw, −3 defeat.
`match_record_result_code(record)`, from the competition statistics (`exe::comp_stats_record_match_result`, on each match). Null record: the box
(line 0x25a) and 0. For (+0x19) > against (+0x1a), signed: 3; draw with goals: 2; goalless draw: 1; defeat: −3 (only
the byte counts: the caller reads al).

Tells whether the match record is a win by a larger margin than the other one, or the same margin with more goals
scored.
`match_record_is_bigger_win(a, b)`, from the club records after each match (0x444930) and from the competition ones
(0x49fb93): 1 if `a` is a win (goals +0x19 > +0x1a, signed bytes) by a larger margin than that of `b`, or equal with
more goals scored. Null record: the original routine ("Error" box, 0).

Tells whether the match record is a defeat by a larger margin than the other one, or the same margin with more goals
conceded.
`match_record_is_bigger_defeat(a, b)`, from the club records after each match (0x444930): 1 if `a` is a defeat
(+0x19 < +0x1a) by a larger margin than that of `b`, or equal with more goals conceded. Null record: the original
routine ("Error" box, 0).

The scout manager's daily update, on day slice 2: prunes the scouting requests (non-human club, player already at
the club, older than a year, 3 reports, injured); a request older than 30 days becomes up to 3 reports from the
manager's scouts covering the player's nation and leaves; then the reports, the request order and one search tick on
every human manager list.
Ret 0; SEH frame for the local list and the dates: `SCOUT_MANAGER::daily_update()`, from the day (only on slice 2 of
the day, `[0xae2c88]`; otherwise 0). Prunes the scouting requests (+0x5c, count +0x64, 0x11 bytes; the removed one
gets the last one), and the processed request becomes up to 3 reports from the scouts of the club's manager (of the
10 lists, `scout_record`, the one that covers the player's nation, `scout_covers_nation`): `exe::player_search_report_on_player` with −1000, mode 1, and the record
(0x67 bytes) goes into the local list if byte +0x66 ended ≥ 0. Then the reports (`send_scout_reports`), the request order
(`exe::crt_qsort` with 0x7fc270) and one search (`exe::player_search_run_scout_day`) on each of the 10 lists of the human managers (the last 16
persons with +0x5f = 1). Returns 1.

Copies the list records into an array, sorts it and sends one news item per run of the same player and club.
Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::send_scout_reports(list)`, from the scouts' day (`scout_manager_daily_update`) and from the search (`scout_manager_scout_match`).
With the list not empty (+0 count): a vector of count × 0x67 (`exe::crt_malloc`; out of memory, the box at line 0x7dd) with
copies of the records, sorted (`exe::crt_qsort` with 0x7fc2a0); each consecutive group of the same player (+0x2b) and the
same club (+0x50) becomes a report news item (`send_scout_report_news` with the first one and how many). Frees the vector
(`exe::crt_free`). The list is left with its cursor at the start.

Sends the 0x138e news item with up to 3 records, the scout, the match and the player's strengths for the club, to
the club's manager.
Ret 8; SEH frame for the local news item: `SCOUT_MANAGER::send_scout_report_news(record, count)`, from the reports
(`send_scout_reports`). News 0x138e (`construct_news_item`): count (up to 3), +0x66, the scout (`exe::write_staff_name_ref_to_news` with +0x1f), +0x59, +0x5a, club
+0x50, the match data (0x7e4de0), +0x5e, +0x62, +0x58, +0x54, from each of the records (+0x37 + 0x67 × k) +0xc, +0,
+4, +8 and +0x26 + 8 × +0x25, 0x420e9 and the player's (+0x2b) strengths for the club (`staff_get_player_strength_flags`); goes to the club's
manager (`send_to_club_manager`).

Tells whether the current search of the current human manager session has no club (+0x191 = −2).
Ret 0: `SCOUT_MANAGER::current_search_has_no_club()`, from the search screens (0x482a9b). The session of the human
manager whose turn it is (`[this + 0xc + 4 × index]`): the current search (the signed byte at +0 of the session)
without a club (+0x191 = −2). No manager or no session: 0; index out of range: the box (line 0x454; the original)
and 0.

Tells whether one of the 10 searches of the current human manager session is for the club.
Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::is_club_in_session_searches(club)`, from the screens (0x482aaf, 0x483040, 0x7b34e1). Any of
the 10 searches of the session of the human manager whose turn it is has the club (+0x191 = +0 of the club): 1. No
manager or no session: 0; index out of range: the box (line 0x480; the original) and 0.

The scouts at the match: for each human manager, the 10 scouts in a randomly drawn order; one for the playing club
starts the assignment, and each watches the match; at the end the reports go out.
Ret 8; SEH frame for the local LLIST `exe::new_llist`/`exe::drop_llist`: `SCOUT_MANAGER::scout_match(fixture, result)`, from the
closing of the day's match (`close_day_match`, Rust). For each of the last 16 person records (`[0xae23bc]`, 0x6e bytes, from
the last backwards) with +0x5f = 1 (the human manager): in a zeroed vector of 10 marks (`exe::crt_calloc`), the 10 scouts in
a random order (`exe::utils_random` of 10 until an unmarked one is found); each one's record (`scout_record`) with +0x19d, in a
fixture with flags +0x40 and +0x41 and of the manager's club (+0x39 = +0x1c or +0x20 of the fixture), starts the
scouting (`exe::player_search_start_scout_assignment` with −1, −1, −1, 0, 1); and watches the match (`player_search_scout_match`, the reports into the local list). The
vector is freed (`exe::crt_free`). Finally the reports go out (`send_scout_reports`) and the list is destroyed. Returns 1.

Returns the human manager's searches edit session.
Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::get_edit_session(manager)`, from building the search's known players (0x7afeb7). The human
manager's edit session (+0xc + 4 × index). No manager or index out of range: the box (lines 0xde and 0xe8; the
original) and 0.

Stores the human manager's searches edit session and returns 1.
Ret 8: `SCOUT_MANAGER::set_edit_session(session, manager)`, from the search screens (0x8085bc, 0x812d88...). Writes
the session into +0xc + 4 × the manager's index and returns 1. No manager or index out of range: the box (lines 0xb8
and 0xc2; the original) and 0.

Returns the list selected by the human manager (null: the current one).
Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::get_selected_list(manager)`, from the search screens (0x804248). The list chosen by the human
manager (byte at +0x4c + index). No manager or outside 0..15: the original routine ("Error" box, 0xff).

Stores the list selected by the human manager (null: the current one).
Ret 8: `SCOUT_MANAGER::set_selected_list(list, manager)`, from the search screens (0x804460). Writes the chosen list
(byte) into +0x4c + the human manager's index and returns 1. No manager or outside 0..15: the original routine
("Error" box, 0).

Tells whether the fixture has a watched club or an available player with a scout request (at the club or national
side, not loaned out, injured, suspended or barred, and not yet played).
Ret 4: `SCOUT_MANAGER::fixture_has_scouted_player(fixture)` (from match_without_human `exe::match_day_can_quick_simulate`): negative
competition (+0), 0. A club of the watched list (static LLIST 0xb74438, cursor reset; +0 of the item) equal to +0xc
or +0x10 of the fixture, 1. Then the scouting requests (`[this+0x5c]`, 0x11 bytes, the person at +4, count
`[this+0x64]`, reread on each step): a person whose club (+0x39) or national side (+0x24) is one of the two in the
fixture (+0x1c first, then +0x20), who is not loaned out (`player_needs_work_permit`, outside a national side `exe::database_is_national_team`), nor injured

Tells whether the club can scout the nation: a poor (balance < 1,000,000) and small (reputation < 5000) club outside

Tells whether the club (or the current human's) asked to scout the player, with fewer than 3 reports and, if asked,
with the date already due.
Ret 0xc: `SCOUT_MANAGER::has_scout_request(player, club, only_due)`: whether the club (null: that of the human whose

The original's local date (`exe::date_date_54a110`) only fills the key after the pair.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::update_coach_assignments(club, manager)`, called by the coach hirings and departures (`exe::contract_manager_resolve_contract_offers`,
`sign_contract`, `exe::transfer_manager_move_player_to_club`, the regen `player_regen_retire_from_non_playing_staff`) and by the club change (`reassign_squad_schedules`): updates the six training staff slots of
the human manager and recomputes each category rating.
Without a manager and with a club without a human (`exe::human_manager_is_human_club` with 1, 1, 0, 0), or a national side club (`exe::database_is_national_team`):
nothing. A null manager: the club's (+0xcf). The human's exe::training_manager_get_coach_assignments(`get_coach_assignments`, six 9-byte slots): (1) the slot whose
coach has no non-player sheet (+0x69) or is neither the assistant (`database_get_club_assistant`) nor one of the 5 coaches (`database_get_club_coaches`) is
emptied; (2) the assistant and the coaches with a sheet that are not in the slots go into the first empty one with
all five categories (0x01010101 and 1); (3) each flagged category gets its rating: 0 (goalkeepers, sheet +0x10)
(chance − sheet +0x12 + 21) / 2; 1 (tactics, +0x21 and +0x10) (chance + chance + +0x12) / 3; 2 (+0x10) (chance +
+0xe + +0x12) / 3; 3 (+0x10) (chance + +0x12) / 2; 4 (+0x11) the chance (divisions truncated toward zero; the chance
from `exe::non_player_attribute_rating`), the signed byte divided by the divisor for the number of flagged categories (1.0 to 2.0, float),
truncated and clamped to 1..20.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::reassign_squad_schedules(manager, old, new)`, when the human manager changes club (`remove_staff_from_club` and
0x68f9c0/0x69ebc0, manager_manager.cpp): reassigns the training schedules of the old and new squads.
The old club's squad (`database_collect_club_squad`, 50): each valid person (id below [0xae2364]) gets load 50 (`set_training_load`) and slot 6
(goalkeeper with 15 or more, sheet +0xf) or 1 in the training entry; without a sheet, the box (line 0x34c). With a
new club: of the manager's ten schedules, the last one of type 6 (+0x15) is the goalkeepers' and the last one of
type 1 the general one; each player of the new squad with a sheet goes to the goalkeepers' schedule (goalkeeper with
15 or more, if there is one), otherwise the general one (if there is one), otherwise slot 1, with the schedule's
load (`get_training_load`) on the fitness sheet; finally the training staff (`update_coach_assignments` with the new club and the manager).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::update_player_training(person, skip)`, called by the player initialisation for the match
(`exe::match_player_setup`, match_man.cpp, with 0: every player of every match), by a new injury (`add_injury`) and by the screens:
brings the player's training weeks up to date (up to 30).
A null person (line 0x18a), without the sheet (0x195) or without a schedule (`get_player_schedule` null, 0x1a3): the "Error" box;
an id from [0xae2364] on: nothing. A player of a human manager's club without flag 0x20 in +5 of the training entry:
the flag, the schedule slot (the goalkeepers' one, type 6, for a goalkeeper with 15 or more; otherwise the general
one, type 1; otherwise 1) and its load (`get_training_load`) on the fitness sheet (`set_training_load`). Weeks = training week (+0x688d) −
the entry's (+1); none and without `skip`: nothing. With the flag and the club no longer with a human manager:
clears the flag, load 50, slot 6 or 1 and the position training stops (`exe::training_manager_set_position_training_rate` with 0).
Up to 30 weeks: brings the entry up to date; each category (0..4) has the weight level × 2 + 60 + (coach factor −
100) / 5 (0..200) and, per week, progress rolls: up 1 with weight above 100, draw(210 − weight) < 20, value below
(+0x58) / 3 and draw(|value| × 2 + 14) < 10; otherwise down 1 with weight below 110, draw(weight + 60) < 20, value
above −7 and above (+0x5b) / 3 − 6 and the same last draw (goalkeeper with 19 or more: only with draw(4), or draw(2)
in category 4, at zero).
The position training items (`find_position_training`, 8-byte items: +4 the mask, +6 the rating, +7 the rate) advance per week (or
once, with `skip` in the mask): with a positive rate, draw(rate) < 5 gives rating + 2 (up to 20) and the player may
complain (club contract `exe::contract_manager_get_contract_for_club` without 0x8000 in +0x45: by a rate above 50 or an aptitude `get_position_aptitude` below 12, with
+0x5b below 15, draw(+0x5b) < 10 and no injury `get_player_injury_status`: flag 0x8000 (`exe::staff_contract_apply_event_flags`), −5 on +0x44 (−100..100) and
`exe::news_post_player_unhappy_with_training`); with a negative rate, draw(−rate) < 5 gives rating − 2 and, below 1, the item ends (rate 0, rating 1). It
applies the progress (`apply_training_progress`) and, with finished items, removes them from the list (the last one into the gap) and
re-sorts (qsort `exe::crt_qsort` with 0x8b4e00).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_player_schedule(person)`, called by the people's daily update (game_daily_staff_update
0x5ce2d0), by `game_check_players_missing_training` and by update_player_training (`update_player_training`): returns the player's training schedule.
A null person or one without the sheet: the "Error" box (line 0x6ad) and 0. At a human manager's club (contract
`exe::contract_manager_get_contract`, kept in [0xae1080]; manager +0xcf among the last 16 ids): injured (0x62c400 = 2), the human's schedule 1,
this + 0x4d8 + 0x60e × ([0xae2364] − id − 1); otherwise the one of the training entry's slot (+0, outside 0..9 slot
1); outside the 16, the box (line 0x68f) and 0. Otherwise: injured, schedule 0 (this); otherwise this + 0x9b × slot
(signed).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::remove_or_restore_training_progress(person, restore)`: takes the progress stored in the training
entry off the attributes or puts it back, around the player attribute normalisations (`staff_normalise_player_attributes` and `staff_normalise_player_physical_attributes`: on
ageing in the people's daily update 0x5ce2d0, in the young regen `regenerate_as_youth_player` and on load), which take the progress off
before and put it back after.
A null person or one without the sheet: the "Error" box (line 0x621). Taking off (`restore` = 0): keeps the five
progress nibbles of the training entry in 0xde1f3c..0xde1f40 (category 3, 2, 4, 0, 1) and applies the negated
progress (`apply_training_progress`); restoring: applies the kept one.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_training_attribute_change(person, attribute)`, called by the training screen (0x8b8184): how
much the training progress adds to an attribute: the attribute (`staff_get_player_attribute`) minus the same attribute without the
training progress (it applies the negated progress, reads, and reapplies the progress), in al. A null person or one
without the sheet: the "Error" box (line 0x657) and 0.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_position_aptitude(person, mask)` (`this` not used), called by update_player_training
(`update_player_training`, the position training complaint) and by set_position_training_rate (`exe::training_manager_set_position_training_rate`): the player's aptitude to
learn a position or side: the average of the adaptability (person's +0x56) and the attributes the position needs
(ratings 1 to 20 through `player_attribute_rating` over the sheet +0x61).
Goalkeeper (1) +0x39, +0x2a and +0x35, over 4; defence (2, 4) +0x3e, +0x39 and +0x32, over 4; midfield and attack
(8, 0x10, 0x20) +0x37, +0x32, +0x40 and +0x3f, over 5; 0x40 +0x33, +0x27, +0x40 and +0x36, over 5; 0x80 +0x30, over
2; 0x200 only the adaptability (in al, the upper bytes with the mask); 0x800 +0x3b, over 2 (truncated divisions).
Any other mask: the "Error" box (line 0x945) and 0.

`TRAINING_SCHEDULE::set_type(slot, type)`: stores the schedule's slot and type and its five category levels from the
type's mix.
The slot (signed, as a dword) at +0, the type at +0x15 and the five category levels (+4..+8) by the type's mix (jump
table 0x8b4f08): 1 general (25 in the first four), 2 to 5 one category at 50 and the others at 10, 6 goalkeepers (50
in the fifth, 0 in the third), 0 and 7 no training (all 0); outside 0..=7 (the −1 of the human's first slot) only
the slot and the type. Called by set_default_schedules (`set_default_schedules`, 167 times at the start of the game) and by the
training screens.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::set_default_schedules()`, called by the constructor (0x8b0ec0) in a new game (without
training.dat): sets up the computer's seven schedules and the ten schedules of each of the 16 human managers, then
gives the default names.
The computer's seven schedules (0x9b bytes each from this; type k in slot k: the computer trains through slot 1,
general, and slot 6, goalkeepers, according to the player's training entry) and, for each of the 16 human managers
(person [0xae2364] − h − 1, 0x6e-byte record in [0xae23bc]), the ten schedules: slots 0 to 5 computed here (types
−1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4), 6 to 9 through `get_manager_schedule` (types 5, 6, 7, 7). At the end the default names (`exe::training_manager_set_default_schedule_names`). Called by
address (`set_type` and `get_manager_schedule` in this batch).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_coaching_factor(club, category)`, called by TRAINING_MANAGER::update_player_training
(`update_player_training`, five times per player in each training update; the value goes in as (factor − 100) / 5 into the weight of
the progress roll): the coaching factor of a training category.
A null club: 0. Without a manager (+0xcf) or with a computer manager (id below [0xae2364] − 16): 100 (eax carries
the upper 16 bits of the manager pointer, as in the original). A human manager: his staff (`get_coach_assignments`, six 9-byte
slots: id −1 is an empty slot, the category rating at +4 + category); with n coaches with a rating, the sum (16
bits) divided by the nth divisor and truncated (_ftol 0x945640), × 40/7 (0x970400) and truncated; below 50, 50. Hot
on the computer branch: no counter there.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_coach_assignments(manager)`: returns the training staff table (six 9-byte slots) of one of
the 16 human managers, at this + 0x652d + 54 × ([0xae2364] − id − 1).
A null manager: the "Error" box (line 0xa20) and 0; outside the 16 human managers: the box (line 0xa2a) and 0.

`TRAINING_SCHEDULE::get_training_load()`: the schedule's load from its five category levels (+4..+8, signed) with
fixed weights, up to 100.
trunc(+8 × 0.5) − trunc(+4 × −1.3) − trunc(+7 × −0.5) − trunc(+6 × −0.5) − trunc(+5 × −0.5) (constants 0x968968,
0x96f878, 0x969540; _ftol 0x945640), in 16 bits; from 100 up, 100. Called by update_player_training (`update_player_training`, the
human club's player), by set_player_schedule (0x8b2250) and by reassign_squad_schedules (`reassign_squad_schedules`); it goes to the
fitness sheet (Injury::set_training_load `set_training_load`).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::apply_training_progress(person, d)`, called by update_player_training (`update_player_training`, each player on
each training update) and by `remove_or_restore_training_progress` and `get_training_attribute_change`: adds each category's progress to the player's stored nibble,
moving the category attributes, then handles the trained position or side.
A null person: the "Error" box (line 0x4b3); without the sheet (+0x61): the box (line 0x4ba); an id from [0xae2364]
on: nothing. With the player's 6-byte entry (this +0x651d + 6 × sheet id), each category with progress `d[k]` other
than zero moves its step (progress_step over the stored nibble) on its sheet attributes (those from 1 to 20 by the
step, those from −125 to 125 by six times the step; every two steps the attributes move) and stores the nibble plus
`d[k]`: 3 (+4 high), 0 (+3 low), 2 (+4 low), 1 (+3 high) and 4 (+5 low).
Then the position training (`find_position_training`): with the learning entry at 15 or more, the position or side of the mask goes
to 20 (learnt); below that, it goes back to 1 (training stopped) if more than one position (+0xf..+0x15) or side
(+0x17..+0x19) at 15 or more is still left. Hot: no counter.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::find_position_training(person, &first)`: finds the player's first entry in the sorted position
training list and returns how many are his.
A null person, the "Error" box (line 0x995); a null output, the box (line 0x99c); without the sheet (+0x61), the box
(line 0x9a3): 0. Without flag 0x10 in +5 of the player's training entry (this +0x651d + 6 × sheet id), the position
training mark: 0. Otherwise the binary search (`exe::crt_bsearch`, order 0x8b4e00) of the person's id in the position training
list (this +0x6521, count +0x6525, 8-byte items); not found: 0; found: steps back to the person's first item, stores
it in the output and returns how many consecutive ones are hers.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::advance_week_counter(&day)`, every day from the day loop (game_main_day_loop 0x5cccd0, with the
day of the year of the game date 0xae2c90): on a day that is a multiple of 7 (signed remainder), the training week
(+0x688d, 16 bits) goes up by 1; update_player_training (`update_player_training`) catches up each player with the missing weeks.
Returns day / 7 (the caller does not read it).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::init_player_entries()`, called by the constructor (0x8b0ec0) in a new game: allocates the 6-byte
training entry of every player sheet and puts goalkeepers on schedule 6 and the others on 1.
Allocates (calloc `exe::crt_calloc`) the 6-byte training entries, one per player sheet ([0xae236c] sheets of 0x46 bytes in
[0xae23c4], the sheet by its id +0), at this + 0x651d; without memory, the box (line 0x6e3) and it returns. In each
entry it clears bit 0x20 of +5 and sets the schedule slot (+0): 6 (goalkeepers) with a goalkeeping rating (+0xf,
signed) of 15 or more, otherwise 1 (general). Each player's first training update (`update_player_training`, which only afterwards
redoes the slot of the computer's players) and all of the human club's training use this slot.
